'''Gore:''' {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} {{legend0|#3933e5|80–90%}} | title = U.S. Senator | before_election = [[Al Gore]] | before_party = Democratic Party (United States) | after_election = [[Al Gore]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsTN}} The '''1990 United States Senate election in Tennessee''' was held on November 6, 1990, to select the [[United States Senate|U.S. senator]] from the state of [[Tennessee]]. Incumbent Senator [[Al Gore]] of the [[Democratic Party (US)|Democratic Party]] defeated challenger William R. Hawkins of the [[Republican Party (US)|Republican Party]], winning a second term. The election had a turnout rate of just over 20% of registered voters. Gore won in a landslide with over 67% of the vote, improving on his 1984 margin and winning all of the state's counties. Hawkins's campaign was poorly funded and relatively unknown, compared to Gore, who was incredibly popular within the state and began the race with over a million dollars in campaign funds. Gore was expected to easily win re-election, and the election cycle was labeled "boring". Issues for the campaign included fiscal responsibility and Gore's liberal voting record. As of 2026, this was the last time the Democrats won a U.S. Senate election in Tennessee, and the last Tennessee U.S. Senate race in which any candidate won every county. == Background == {{Main|1984 United States presidential election in Tennessee}} In 1984, despite [[Ronald Reagan]]'s [[1984 United States presidential election|landslide victory]] in the concurrent presidential election,{{Cite news |last=Raines |first=Howell |date=November 7, 1984 |title=Reagan Wins By a Landslide, Sweeping at Least 48 States; G.O.P. Gains Strength in House |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/reagan-wins-by-a-landslide-sweeping-at-least-48-states-gop-gains.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825144938/http://www.nytimes.com/1984/11/07/politics/07REAG.html?pagewanted=1 |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |access-date=March 12, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Al Gore flipped an open Senate seat held by retiring Republican [[Howard Baker]],{{Cite news |date=November 7, 1984 |title=Senate Dems avoid rout, but GOP still controls |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/263349084/ |access-date=September 9, 2025 |work=[[Journal and Courier]] |page=A8 |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} defeating Republican [[Victor Ashe]] with a little over 60% of the vote. By contrast, Reagan won Tennessee in the presidential election with 58% of the vote to 42% for Democratic candidate [[Walter Mondale]].{{Cite web |last=Ladd |first=Thomas E. |date=May 1, 1985 |title=Statistics of the Presidential and Congressional election of November 6, 1984 |url=https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electionInfo/1984election.pdf |access-date=April 21, 2025 |website=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives|Clerk of the House of Representatives]] |pages=54-55}} The 1990 election was held as part of the [[United States midterm election|midterm election cycle]] of Republican President [[George H. W. Bush]]'s term.{{Cite news |last1=Dewar |first1=Helen |last2=Yang |first2=John E. |date=November 6, 1990 |title=The Senate Incumbents Win Control Remains with Democrats |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/1990/11/07/the-senate/88a317b4-abae-4a7c-9a3c-f65fe6b52b54/ |access-date=March 12, 2025 |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]}} Historically, the president's party struggles during the midterms.{{Cite news |last=Elving |first=Ron |date=November 13, 2022 |title=The midterms didn't produce a wave. Here's what that's meant historically |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/11/13/1136103595/the-midterms-didnt-produce-a-wave-heres-what-thats-meant-historically |access-date=April 1, 2025 |work=[[NPR]] |language=en}} Gore was one of several politicians who were seen as likely candidates for the 1992 Democratic presidential nomination up for reelection.{{Cite news |last=Benedetto |first=Richard |date=May 14, 1990 |title=Democrats slow to take aim at Bush |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/239988627/ |access-date=September 11, 2025 |work=[[Argus-Leader]] |page=6A}} ==Candidates and primaries == * [[Al Gore]] ([[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]]), incumbent [[United States Senate|Senator]] * William R. Hawkins ([[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]]), conservative author Primary elections were held on August 2, 1990. Just under 25% of Tennessee's 2.5 million registered voters voted in the primary elections. State elections coordinator Will Burns said the turnout rate was "pretty dismal".{{Cite news |last=Myers |first=Hortense |date=August 31, 1990 |title=Tennessee election results now official; no surprises |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/773655430/ |access-date=September 9, 2025 |work=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |page=A10 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} === Democratic primary === * Al Gore, incumbent Senator{{Cite news |last=Humphrey |first=Tom |date=August 8, 1990 |title=Gore foe vows 'unorthodox campaign' |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/774959287/ |access-date=April 21, 2025 |work=[[The Knoxville News-Sentinel]] |pages=A6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} After winning his first term in a landslide victory, Gore decided to run for a second. He was unopposed in the Democratic primary. Writing for ''[[The Commercial Appeal]]'', Terry Keeter credited the lack of competition to the margin of Gore's victory in the 1984 senate election.{{Cite news |last=Keeter |first=Terry |date=August 2, 1990 |title=Three bidding to unseat Gore |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/773644938/ |access-date=April 21, 2025 |work=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |pages=J10 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Gore received almost 480,000 votes, with 54 votes cast for [[Write-in candidate|write-in candidates]]. {{Election box begin no change |title=1990 United States Senate election in Tennessee Democratic primary}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party=Democratic Party (United States) |candidate=Al Gore (incumbent) |votes=479,961 |percentage=99.99%}} {{Election box write-in with party link no change | votes = 54 | percentage = 0.01% }} {{Election box total no change |votes=480,015 |percentage=100.00%}} {{Election box end}} === Republican primary === *Ralph H. Brown, retiree with no political experience *Patrick K. Hales, unsuccessful candidate for the [[Tennessee Public Service Commission]] in 1986 *William R. Hawkins, conservative author Former Governor [[Lamar Alexander]], who was very popular in the state, was seen as the only person who could successfully oust Gore. However, he declined to run in favor of being president of the [[University of Tennessee]]. Hawkins ran after being approached by the Tennessee Conservative Union. He felt that Gore was "the most liberal Senator from the south" and did not properly represent the views of Tennesseans.{{Cite news |date=July 29, 1990 |title=Three GOP candidates vie for right to challenge Gore |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/1003716686/ |access-date=April 21, 2025 |work=Elizabethton Star |pages=2A |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} He described similarities between the voting records of Gore and his father, [[Albert Gore Sr.]],{{Cite news |last=Banks |first=Robert |date=July 26, 1990 |title=GOP Senate hopeful labels Gore a 'Liberal' |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/594615671 |access-date=June 3, 2025 |work=[[Kingsport Times-News]] |page=3B |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} noting that Gore Sr. had lost reelection. Hawkins' primary had a total budget of $3,000. Brown felt that even if he won the nomination he would not be able to defeat Gore in the general election. Despite this he felt it would give him a platform to publicize his beliefs. Hales ran because he felt Gore was "out of touch" with his fellow Tennesseans. After the primary, Hales said he was advised against running.{{Cite news |last=Rawlins |first=Bill |date=September 9, 1990 |title=Tenn. GOP faces future when leadership gathers |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/594649464/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210718195518/https://www.deseret.com/1994/10/16/19136960/bush-considered-quayle-a-liability-in-92-book-says |archive-date=July 18, 2021 |access-date=September 4, 2025 |work=[[Kingsport Times-News]] |page=6B |via=[[Newspapers.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Despite Gore being expected to easily win the general election, the primary was very closely contested. Hawkins defeated Brown by a very narrow margin, though both received over 20,000 more votes than Hale. [[2002 United States Senate election in Tennessee|Twelve years later]], Alexander would win Gore's seat in 2002 {{Election box begin no change |title=1990 United States Senate election in Tennessee Republican primary}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party=Republican Party (United States) |candidate=William R. Hawkins |votes=54,317 |percentage=38.86%}} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |party=Republican Party (United States) |candidate=Ralph Brown |votes=53,873 |percentage=38.54%}} {{Election box candidate with party link no change |party=Republican Party (United States) |candidate=Patrick K. Hales |votes=31,515 |percentage=22.55%}} {{Election box write-in with party link no change | votes = 70 | percentage = 0.05% }} {{Election box total no change |votes=139,775 |percentage=100.00%}} {{Election box end}} == General election == Hawkins's campaign was poorly funded;{{Cite news |last=Wade |first=Paula |date=November 4, 1990 |title=Gore in Memphis pulpits, on TV for finale |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/773722228/ |access-date=June 3, 2025 |work=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |page=B6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}}{{Cite news |date=November 7, 1990 |title=McWherter, Gore coast to victories |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/963927131/ |access-date=April 21, 2025 |work=[[Bristol Herald Courier]] |pages=1A, 8A |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} he only had $3,000 to fund his primary run, while Gore had begun the campaign with around $1,000,000. Two weeks before election day Hawkins had raised $12,000 to Gore's $2,000,000.{{Cite news |date=October 29, 1990 |title=Even GOP activists don't know Senate nominee |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/594651122/ |access-date=April 27, 2025 |work=[[Kingsport Times-News]] |pages=2A |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Hawkins' campaign ended with zero cash on hand while Gore had just over $700,000 left.{{Cite web |title=1990 Election United States Senate – Tennessee |url=https://www.fec.gov/data/elections/senate/TN/1990/ |access-date=May 23, 2025 |website=[[Federal Election Commission]] |language=en}} Hawkins stated that he wanted to run the most "issue-orientated campaign Tennessee has ever seen." He criticized Gore's liberal views, including his stance on the [[Capital punishment in the United States|death penalty]] and his support for the [[Civil Rights Act of 1990]]. Despite Gore being more pro-military than most Democrats, Hawkins criticized him for being "soft on defense".{{Cite news |last=Daughtrey |first=Larry |date=August 19, 1990 |title=One way to get rid of the mayor |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/113155891/? |access-date=June 4, 2025 |work=[[The Tennessean]] |page=1G |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Hawkins noted that the [[federal deficit]] had increased under policy's that Gore had voted for. He stated that if elected he would work to cut taxes and reduce government spending. The staff of ''[[The Jackson Sun]]'' characterized Tennessee's election cycle as boring, noting the likelihood of Gore and incumbent Governor [[Ned McWherter]] being reelected, writing, "the gubernatorial and senatorial races are a yawn".{{Cite news |last=Reed |first=Mary S. |date=November 4, 1990 |title=State races drawn yawn from voters |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/283809298/ |access-date=April 22, 2025 |work=[[The Jackson Sun]] |page= |pages=1A, 3A}} Republican Representative [[Don Sundquist]] felt that the Hawkins was a weak candidate and that Republicans would likely have a better chance of taking the seat in the 1996 election.{{Cite news |last=Brosnan |first=James W. |date=November 4, 1990 |title=An easy election ride doesn't make Sundquist feel easy about future |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/773722263/ |access-date=May 26, 2025 |work=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |pages=B11, B13 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} On October 29, 1990, roughly two weeks before election day, Hawkins admitted that his campaign "failed to generate excitement" and acknowledged the relative obscurity of his campaign even within Republican groups. However, the staff of ''[[The Commercial Appeal]]'' noted that Gore would have some difficulty with his bid due to the conservative lean of Tennessee and his liberal voting record.{{Cite news |date=November 6, 1990 |title=Don't give up / Voters can find a few good contests |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/773723173/ |access-date=May 20, 2025 |work=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |pages=A10}} Gore was unable to make in person campaign visits for much of the race due to his role in Congress. The campaign ran a single sixty second television advertisement. In the final few days of the campaign, Gore visited several locations in [[Memphis, Tennessee]] and ran a half hour long [[television special]] in all major markets throughout the state. Gore's press secretary said the special cost around $20,000-$30,000 and was produced by the firm Squier-Eskew-Knapp advertising firm. On the contrary, Hawkins canceled his planned statewide press conferences and was unable to air radio ads he had recorded due to budgetary constraints. Hawkins had planned to host a fundraising dinner, however he had to cancel the dinner after the organizer of the event died. === Results === The election was held on November 6, 1990.{{Cite news |last=Espo |first=David |date=November 7, 1990 |title=Demos win Texas, Florida, four other Governships; Helms wins |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/344952161/ |access-date=April 21, 2025 |work=[[The Times and Democrat]] |pages=A1, A4 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Gore, like most incumbents in the [[1990 United States Senate elections]], was reelected to another term. He won in a landslide,{{Cite news |last=Komarow |first=Steve |date=November 7, 1990 |title=Helms triumphs over Gnatt in N.C. Senate race |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/112819132/ |access-date=May 20, 2025 |work=[[The Tennessean]] |pages=11A |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} receiving over 67 percent of the vote,{{Cite web |last=Liep |first=Dave |title=1990 Senatorial General Election Results – Tennessee |url=http://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?year=1990&fips=47&off=3&class=2&elect=0&f=1 |access-date=April 21, 2025 |website=[[Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections]]}} an improvement on his previous margin of victory.{{Cite web |last=Thomas |first=Richard C. |date=June 1985 |title=Federal Elections 84 Election Results for U.S. President, U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives |url=https://www.fec.gov/resources/cms-content/documents/federalelections84.pdf |access-date=May 24, 2025 |website=[[Federal Election Commission]] |page=23}} [[Independent politician|Independent]] candidates Charles Gordon Vick and Bill Jacox both received around 1% of the vote each. A total of 109 votes were cast for write-in candidates. The election had a turnout rate of slightly over 20% of registered voters casting ballots, a similar level to the concurrent [[1990 Tennessee gubernatorial election|gubernatorial election]].{{Cite web |last=Leip |first=Dave |title=1990 Gubernatorial General Election Results – Tennessee |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/state.php?fips=47&year=1990&f=0&off=5&elect=0 |access-date=May 26, 2025 |website=[[Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections]]}} Low voter turnout was projected due to the lack of major opposition in the Senate and Gubernatorial elections. However, the turnout rate was higher than expected.{{Cite news |last=Weston |first=Alan |date=November 7, 1990 |title=McWherter, Gore win re-election |url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/594767565/ |access-date=September 9, 2025 |work=[[Kingsport Times-News]] |pages=A1–A2 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} Gore won all 95 of the state's counties. His best performance was in [[Trousdale County]], where he won 88 percent of the vote to Hawkins' 10 percent. Hawkins' best performance was in [[Monroe County, Tennessee|Monroe County]] where he won around 40 percent of the vote to Gore's 57 percent. Gore over performed McWherter's margin in the gubernatorial race by around seven percent, although he received a lower number of votes. Hawkins under performed Republican gubernatorial candidate Dwight Henry.{{Election box begin no change | title = 1990 United States Senate election in Tennessee{{cite web |title=Statistics of the Congressional Election of November 6, 1990 |url=https://clerk.house.gov/member_info/electioninfo/1990election.pdf |publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives]] |date=April 29, 1991 |access-date= |format=PDF}}}} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change | party = Democratic Party (United States) | candidate = [[Al Gore]] (incumbent) | votes = 530,898 | percentage = 67.73% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change | party = Republican Party (United States) | candidate = William R. 1991, Gore was sworn in to the [[102nd United States Congress]] by then-Vice President [[Dan Quayle]] alongside his fellow senators-elect.{{Cite video |url=https://www.c-span.org/program/senate-highlight/swearing-in-of-senate-members/10810 |title=Swearing-In of Senate Members |date=January 3, 1991 |type=Video |publisher=[[C-SPAN]] |time=5:27}} After being elected [[Vice President of the United States|vice president]] in the [[1992 United States presidential election|1992 presidential election]], Gore resigned from his Senate seat on January 2, 1993. [[Harlan Mathews]] was appointed to replace him by Governor [[Ned McWherter]].{{Cite web |date=December 29, 1992 |title=Gore's Senate replacement named |url=https://www.deseret.com/1992/12/29/19023938/gore-s-senate-replacement-named/ |access-date=May 19, 2025 |website=[[Deseret News]] |language=en}} In the [[1994 United States Senate special election in Tennessee|1994 special election]] for the seat, the remainder of Gore's term was won by Republican [[Fred Thompson]], who defeated Democratic Representative [[Jim Cooper]] for [[Tennessee's 4th congressional district]].{{Cite web |last=Brosnan |first=James W. |date=September 18, 2007 |title=What's the truck got to do with it? |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2007/09/whats-the-truck-got-to-do-with-it-005867 |access-date=May 19, 2025 |website=[[Politico]] |language=en}} As of the [[2024 United States Senate elections|2024 election cycle]], this was the last time the Democrats won a Senate election in Tennessee.{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Sarah Grace |date=November 6, 2024 |title=Marsha Blackburn tops Gloria Johnson, wins re-election |url=https://nashvillebanner.com/2024/11/05/marsha-blackburn-re-elected-senate-seat/ |access-date=April 16, 2025 |website=[[Nashville Banner]] |language=en-US}} It is the most recent Senate election in Tennessee in which several counties, including [[Knox County, Tennessee|Knox County]] and [[Hamilton County, Tennessee|Hamilton County]], voted for the Democratic candidate.{{Cite web |last=Liep |first=Dave |title=Senatorial General Election Map Comparison – Tennessee |url=https://uselectionatlas.org/RESULTS/comparemaps.php?year=2024&fips=47&f=0&off=3&elect=0&class=1 |access-date=April 16, 2025 |website=[[Dave Leip's Atlas of U.S. Presidential Elections]]}} Since the 1994 elections, the Democratic party has struggled in the state.{{Cite web |last=Friedman |first=Adam |date=September 11, 2024 |title=Jim Sasser, Tennessee's last Democratic U.S. senator, dies at 87 • Tennessee Lookout |url=https://tennesseelookout.com/2024/09/11/jim-sasser-tennessees-last-democratic-u-s-senator-dies-at-87/ |access-date=April 16, 2025 |website=Tennessee Lookout |language=en-US}} ==References == {{reflist}} {{1990 United States elections}} {{Al Gore}} [[Category:1990 elections in Tennessee]] [[Category:1990 United States Senate elections|Tennessee]] [[Category:United States Senate elections in Tennessee|1990]] [[Category:Al Gore]]
